# Introduction

Wine quality is associated with various physicochemical characteristics, including acidity, residual sugar, chloride concentration, sulfur dioxide levels, density, sulphates, and alcohol content. These characteristics provide measurable information about the chemical composition of wine and may vary between red and white wines. The UCI Wine Quality Dataset contains physicochemical measurements and sensory quality scores for Portuguese Vinho Verde wines, providing a basis for investigating relationships among these variables and differences between wine types (Cortez et al., 2009).

This study aims to investigate the physicochemical characteristics of red and white wines through exploratory data analysis and three multivariate statistical techniques: Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA). MANOVA will examine whether the combined physicochemical characteristics differ between red and white wines, while PCA will determine whether the 11 physicochemical variables can be summarized using fewer components while retaining substantial variability. EFA will further investigate the underlying factors that may explain the relationships among these measurements. Through these analyses, the study seeks to develop a clearer understanding of the multivariate structure of wine characteristics and demonstrate the application of statistical methods to real-world data.

# Dataset Description and Preparation

## Dataset Description

This study uses the Wine Quality Dataset, which contains physicochemical measurements of Portuguese Vinho Verde red and white wines. The data are provided in two separate CSV files, one for red wine and another for white wine. Each observation represents a wine sample described by 11 physicochemical variables and a sensory quality score. The two datasets will be combined into a single dataset, with an additional categorical variable named `color` to distinguish red wines from white wines.

The combined dataset will be used for exploratory data analysis and the subsequent multivariate analyses. The `color` variable will serve as the grouping variable for MANOVA, while the 11 physicochemical measurements will be used as the input variables for PCA and EFA. The `quality` score will be retained for descriptive analysis but excluded from PCA and EFA, as required by the study design. Before proceeding, the data will be checked for correct dimensions, missing values, and duplicate observations to establish the dataset's suitability for further analysis.

## Data Import and Combination

The red and white wine datasets are imported separately and then combined by rows. A categorical variable, `color`, is added to identify the wine type. Column names are standardized using the `janitor` package to make the variables easier to reference during analysis.

```{r data-import}
# Define the relative path to the data folder
data_dir <- file.path("..", "data")

red_file <- file.path(data_dir, "winequality-red.csv")
white_file <- file.path(data_dir, "winequality-white.csv")

# Import red wine data
red_wine <- read.csv(red_file, sep = ";") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  dplyr::mutate(color = "Red")

# Import white wine data
white_wine <- read.csv(white_file, sep = ";") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  dplyr::mutate(color = "White")

# Combine datasets
wine_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(red_wine, white_wine) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    color = factor(color, levels = c("Red", "White"))
  )

# Display the first six observations
knitr::kable(
  head(wine_data),
  caption = "First Six Observations of the Combined Wine Dataset",
  digits = 3,
  format = "html",
  table.attr = 'style="width:100%; table-layout:fixed;"'
) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = TRUE,
    position = "left",
    font_size = 11
  ) |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "350px")
```

## Missing Values and Duplicate Observations

Missing values and duplicate rows are examined to assess data completeness and identify potential data-quality issues. Exact duplicate rows are counted after combining the datasets and adding the wine-color indicator.

```{r data-quality}
# Count missing values in each variable
missing_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(wine_data),
  Missing_Count = colSums(is.na(wine_data))
) |>
  mutate(
    Missing_Percent = round(
      Missing_Count / nrow(wine_data) * 100,
      3
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  missing_summary,
  caption = "Missing Values by Variable",
  digits = 3,
  booktabs = TRUE
)

# Count exact duplicate rows
duplicate_count <- sum(duplicated(wine_data))

duplicate_summary <- data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Total observations",
    "Exact duplicate rows",
    "Unique rows"
  ),
  Count = c(
    nrow(wine_data),
    duplicate_count,
    nrow(wine_data) - duplicate_count
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  duplicate_summary,
  caption = "Duplicate Observation Check",
  booktabs = TRUE
)
```
